title: SLA tiers by P99 latency & capacity-slab simulator
creator: Rina Patel
description:
Summary: Build and run a capacity-slab simulator that maps reserved GPU slabs to discrete SLA tiers defined by P99 latency guarantees, soft-preemption windows, and burst credit behavior. Purpose is to produce a recommended pricing matrix (per-slab monthly rate + burst credit unit price) and templated contract language for enterprise SQ responses. This experiment focuses on quantifying how slab sizing, overcommit policies, and autoscale grace windows affect delivered P99 latency under realistic mixed workloads and how those trade into price points customers will accept.

Background and motivation: Sales and enterprise contracts have asked for more predictable latency guarantees at enterprise scale without forcing customers into oversized reservations. Current reserved models (flat commit + optional burst credits) lack a clear mapping from capacity reservations to latency targets customers can buy. Engineering needs clear sizing guidance and tier definitions to implement autoscale/fallback policies. Security and procurement require cohesive SQ answers describing preemption/retention behavior, telemetry, and access controls per tier.

Scope and goals:
- Simulator that consumes historical/representative workload traces and outputs per-slab P50/P95/P99 latency distributions, tail latencies under burst events, and token-cost estimates.
- Define 3 SLA tiers: Bronze (best-effort P99 soft SLO), Silver (bounded P99 with burst credits and 99.5% availability), Gold (hard P99 with reserved headroom and priority routing). Exact thresholds to be derived by simulation.
- Produce a pricing matrix: monthly slab price, burst credit unit price, and overage cadence.
- Deliver contract templates and Security Questionnaire (SQ) snippets for each tier describing: preemption policy, data residency, KMS behavior, audit logs and telemetry retention.
- Run tabletop with Sales+Legal on 4 pilot accounts and capture feedback.

Assumptions for simulation:
- Hardware: A100 80GB baseline and 4xV100 equivalent legacy pool.
- Typical request mix: 60% chat (short-turn), 30% embeddings (medium-length sequence), 10% long-form generation.
- Burst pattern: Poisson-arrival burst events (1 major burst/week, short spikes 3x/day).
- Autoscale grace windows: 30s, 90s, 300s (three variants).
- Prefix caching hit rates: 10%-40% tested.

Acceptance criteria:
- Simulator validated against two historical traces (internal benchmark and anonymized customer trace).
- Clear thresholds for three SLA tiers with associated slab sizing guidance (e.g., slab X supports Y concurrent chat sessions at <Z ms P99).
- Draft pricing matrix with target gross margin bands and estimated unit economics by slab.
- Completed SQ language snippets reviewed by Security and Legal and approved for pilot.
- Pilot feedback sessions scheduled and recorded with at least two customers providing commitment-level feedback.

Success metrics:
- Simulator reproducibility: consistent results across runs +/-5% on P99 for given config.
- Sales enablement: pilot customers willing to commit to at least 6-month reservations at proposed pricing for at least one tier.
- Legal/Security signoff on SQ snippets within 2 weeks of draft delivery.

Plan and timeline:
- Week 1 (owner: PM): finalize simulator requirements, collect traces, and align metric definitions.
- Week 2-3 (owner: ENG/Research): build and validate simulator, run initial sweep across slab sizes and autoscale windows.
- Week 4 (owner: PM): analyze results, produce pricing matrix & contract draft, and share with Security/Legal.
- Week 5 (owner: PM/Sales): tabletop with pilot accounts, iterate.
- Week 6 (owner: PM): finalize recommendation and handoff to Pricing and Enablement.

Stakeholders: PM (Rina), Eng lead (Priya Malhotra), Research (Noah Kim), Security (Alicia Gomez), Legal (Evan Brooks), Sales (Caroline Xu).

Artifacts and links:
- Simulator design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/sla-simulator (draft)
- Workload traces bucket: s3://redwood-bench/traces/pm-simulator/
- Initial pricing spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-example-pricing-matrix
- Draft SQ answers: https://drive.redwood.ai/sq/dedicated-sla-snippets.docx

Risks and trade-offs:
- Overfitting simulator to internal traces could understate customer burst behavior; mitigated by sourcing at least one anonymized customer trace.
- Tight P99 targets increase price; we must weigh market appetite for price vs. revenue predictability.
- Security review may require additional product controls per tier that affect cost.

Next steps:
- ENG to prioritize simulator infra under ENG-33445.
- Security to review draft SQ snippets inline by 2025-01-22.
- PM to schedule pilot tabletop meetings with top 4 target accounts by 2025-01-31.
